extracted.intended_audience: litigants, counsel, expert witnesses, and judges participating in civil appellate/patent litigation before the Patent Court of Korea
extracted.subtask_description: Practice and procedural rules for civil appellate litigation (infringement and cancellation/revocation actions) before the Patent Court of Korea, covering hearings, evidence, expert witnesses, document preparation, mediation, and related courtroom management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallel handling of infringement and cancellation actions
rubrics_metrics.description: If both an infringement action and a cancellation of IPTAB decision action involving the same subject (patent, utility model, trademark, or design) are filed together before the Court and litigated by the same parties/attorneys, the Court may examine both actions in parallel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Court may examine the issues of nullification and infringement in a first hearing; if nullification is not recognized the Court may issue an opinion and handle remaining infringement issues in a preparatory hearing and second hearing; if nullification is recognized the Court may issue a judgment on cancellation first and then proceed. The Court may also conduct preparatory proceedings for the two actions in parallel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case management: scheduling and staged hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court sets schedules and may designate deadlines for submission of arguments and evidence on disputed issues (e.g., infringement, claim construction, damages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational example for claim construction: set schedule via case-management video conference, designate deadlines for claim-construction submissions, hold a first hearing directed to claim construction, disclose the Court's opinion orally or in writing, then order parties to prepare for a hearing directed to remaining issues and hold a second hearing before judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court disclosure of opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court may disclose its opinion on disputed issues (e.g., infringement, claim construction) either orally or in writing during the hearing process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure may occur at first or preparatory hearings and is used to focus subsequent evidence/deadlines; disclosure can include an indication of whether nullification is recognized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparatory proceedings for evidence examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court may conduct a preparatory proceeding to discuss evidence-examination procedure and related procedural matters, including via video conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After hearing parties' opinions, the presiding judge may discuss procedural matters via video conference and, if necessary, issue a preparatory order regarding evidence examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application to adduce new evidence in appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: A party applying to adduce new evidence in the appeal proceedings must provide a detailed explanation for failing to submit the evidence in the lower court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Court determines admissibility considering circumstances including whether significant harm to the other party is expected from a delay, or whether an expedited proceeding is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application to adduce identical or similar evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party applies to adduce evidence that is identical or similar in evidentiary purport to evidence already admitted/examined by the lower court, the party must provide a detailed explanation of the need for such evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example includes filing a separate appraisal to impeach a lower-court appraisal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application to adduce evidence previously rejected or withdrawn
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party seeks to adduce evidence that was filed but rejected by the lower court or voluntarily withdrawn previously, the party must provide a detailed explanation of the need for such evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert witness declaration and objectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: A party filing a request for an expert witness shall attach a declaration confirming the expertise and objectivity of the witness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The declaration should enable the Court to confirm the expert's qualifications and impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparatory orders for expert witnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court may issue a preparatory order for examination of an expert witness setting deadlines and limits for the expert's statement, questionnaires, time for examination, and deadlines for submitting evidence to impeach credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orders can specify deadlines for submission of the expert witness statement and a questionnaire for direct examination and limit the time for examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limits on direct examination of expert witnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct examination by the party who requests the expert shall be limited to the scope of the expert witness's statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All materials presented or cited during the direct examination must be submitted as evidence before the date designated for examining the witness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreter procedures for foreign expert witnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: If an expert witness is a foreigner, parties may be accompanied by interpreters for direct and cross-examinations; if a party cannot arrange an interpreter, it must notify the Court 4 weeks before and request designation of an interpreter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court orders to produce documents and materials
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court may order a party to submit documents or materials (including electronic documents) necessary for proving infringement or calculating damages (e.g., accounting books, contracts, tax invoices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Court determines types/scope of materials by comparing adverse impact of lack of access to the requesting party versus adverse impact of disclosure on the producing party. The Court may permit redaction of sensitive personal information or irrelevant portions upon justifiable grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court may request description of materials in possession
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon request, the Court may describe purport of requested materials and facts to be proved and order the other party to submit descriptions and purport of related materials in its possession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court may examine parties/witnesses before ordering production
rubrics_metrics.description: If disputed whether the other party possesses the materials, the Court may examine the parties or witnesses prior to issuing an order for production of materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling refusal to produce materials
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party refuses to produce materials, the Court may request the party provide the materials for the purpose of determining whether a justifiable cause exists for the refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality protections for trade secrets
rubrics_metrics.description: If requested, the Court may order that the requesting party or its counsel keep contents of produced materials confidential by ruling when the materials contain trade secrets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court-conducted appraisal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court may conduct an appraisal if no appraisal was conducted in the lower court, if appraisal is necessary to determine a reasonable royalty or contribution ratio, or if otherwise necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties shall explain to the appraiser matters necessary for appraisal of damages amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and use of technical advisors
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court may designate one or more technical advisors; a preparatory hearing may be held to brief advisors and technical advisors may directly question parties with approval of the presiding judge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a party must supplement an answer to a technical advisor question, the party must submit the supplemental answer in writing by a deadline designated by the presiding judge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of arguments/evidence re: amount of damages (respondent)
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent from whom compensation is sought shall provide specific answers to petitioner's arguments and, where relevant, disclose actual sales periods, quantities sold, unit cost of sales, sales amounts, manufacturing cost, and profit rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity requirements for accounting/financial books evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: If accounting or financial books are submitted, the disclosing party shall attach a written confirmation from the person who prepared the books (for a company: CEO and chief accounting officer) verifying the documents are originals or unmodified copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authenticity is reasonably doubted, the disclosing party shall submit additional documents (bank or financial documents) that are the basis for preparing the books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early mediation referral
rubrics_metrics.description: At or soon after receiving an appeal case, the presiding judge may determine suitability for mediation and refer the case to early mediation proceedings; the mediation judge is normally in charge and may conduct mediation at suitable locations other than the Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After first hearing, the presiding judge may also refer the case to mediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief format: table of contents for long briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: If a brief of 20 or more pages is submitted, a table of contents shall be included at the beginning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Briefs: evidentiary references and technical term handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If evidence supporting an argument is submitted, an evidence number shall be indicated in the corresponding portion of the brief; technical terms should be defined in footnotes and sources identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive briefs should include at the beginning a summary of all offensive and defensive arguments and main evidence (including prior arts). In briefs other than comprehensive briefs, arguments previously made shall not be repeated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step argument requirements in briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments denying inventive step must specify the precise combination relationship of prior arts and the reason for the ease in combining the prior arts; failing to specify may be deemed that the argument was not made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit a feature comparison chart comparing corresponding features of the patented invention and each prior art; specify features of prior arts in detail; if a document contains multiple inventions, identify which invention is asserted; specify person of ordinary skill and level. These requirements also apply to free-to-practice (public domain) defenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written-description argument requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An argument alleging lack of written description in the specification shall specify the applicable legal provision on which the argument is based.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infringement argument specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments regarding infringement must describe infringing products and methods specifically, individually, and factually so enforcement agencies can identify them without separate judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include names and model numbers with drawings/photos attached; descriptions must permit direct comparison with the patented invention and correspond to products/methods actually practiced by the other party. Submit a feature comparison chart comparing the patented invention and the alleged infringing products/methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages argument form and defendant's rebuttal
rubrics_metrics.description: Plaintiff's argument regarding amount of damages shall indicate the applicable legal provision and cite an evidence number for each essential element; defendant's response must include detailed rebuttal and specify actual transferred volumes or profits where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any fact not specifically denied by the defendant may be deemed undisputed. If plaintiff claims damages under Article 128(1) defendant must state actual transferred volume; under Article 128(3) defendant must state actual profit amount and grounds for calculation (sales revenues, expenses, profit margins).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanatory documents for evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Each item of evidence must be briefly described with the purport to be proved therefrom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an item is submitted concerning novelty, inventive step, or free-to-practice technology, it must be clearly specified whether it is submitted as a prior art invention or as evidence of well-known prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentary evidence: foreign language translations
rubrics_metrics.description: Written documents in a foreign language must be submitted with a translation attached; main evidence (e.g., prior arts) shall be submitted with a professional translation; machine translations shall not be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each documentary evidence should indicate a title if one exists or a summary if not (with publication date). A prior art document should be labeled as such (e.g., 'Prior Art 1 Registered Patent Publication No. 0012345').

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentary evidence itemization
rubrics_metrics.description: Each evidence item should contain only a single evidentiary item; related multiple items (e.g., blog postings) should be submitted as separate evidentiary documents or as multi-level numbered exhibits.
